title: MODIFY-guided library screening identifies a cytochrome c variant active in both carbon–boron and carbon–silicon bond formation
summary: Researchers applied MODIFY, an ensemble model combining protein language models and sequence-density models, to design a diverse high-fitness library for Rhodothermus marinus cytochrome c. Experimental screening identified variant MLYPPT, which catalyzed both non-natural borylation and silylation: reported total turnover numbers were 2,880 and 2,740, with enantiomeric ratios of 94:6 and 97:3, respectively. The same library yielded distinct high-performing variants for each reaction.
ai_technology: MODIFY (ML-optimized library design with improved fitness and diversity)
organization: Georgia Institute of Technology; University of Pittsburgh; University of California, Santa Barbara

evidence.tested: Experimental screening identified variant MLYPPT, which catalyzed both non-natural borylation and silylation: reported total turnover numbers were 2,880 and 2,740, with enantiomeric ratios of 94:6 and 97:3, respectively.
evidence.unknown: The C–B and C–Si reactions had previously been demonstrated with separately evolved cytochrome c variants; this finding is the discovery of additional, structurally distinct variants and a generalist MLYPPT catalyst. The reported yields and enantiomeric ratios are from the study's assays; industrial scale-up was not shown.
evidence.ai_role: MODIFY used evolutionary sequence models and protein language models for zero-shot fitness estimates, then co-optimized predicted fitness and residue-level diversity to propose a 1,000-variant library. Researchers synthesized and assayed sampled library members; the model-guided library contained experimentally measured new cytochrome c variants, including MLYPPT with activity in both reactions.
